content.text:
Base directory for this skill: /private/var/folders/bj/h8fqdfp53bv05jk5ml8ml4680000gn/T/builder-vy3ll1f0/.claude/skills/read-brief

# Phase 0: read the brief

`cat inputs.json` names the brief and the tool API, both under `input/`. The brief can have any name and any form: specification, mail, memo, notes, transcript. These two files and `docs/` are the only truth; use nothing from memory.

If `inputs.json` says `"mode": "final"`, the input is a case folder of documents (any language, Turkish for the final): `input/corpus.md` holds the text of every document in reading order (BRIEF.md first, README.md says what each is), the originals are in `input/original/`, `tools` is the machine-readable service contract if there is one (otherwise it is one of the documents), and `base_url` is the mock the tools call: every tool URL is `base_url` plus the contract's path. Files listed under `data` (large tables of records, such as the bank's test customers) are not in the corpus: open the original and look up the customers you need. Documents listed under `visual` (drawings, images, PDFs) you must look at with the Read tool, even when their text is in the corpus: a flow drawing's text lists the boxes and loses the arrows, and the arrows are the rules (which question comes first, what each answer leads to). Turn every decision and branch of a drawing into rules; a rule taken from one has `source` (the file name) and a `note` saying what the drawing shows, instead of a verbatim quote. A later announcement or Q&A answer that changes a rule supersedes it (`refs`). Write every customer-facing sentence, and every `wording` rule, in the language of the documents.

**Time box (the harness tells you the minutes; the whole phase is about a quarter of the build):** read the newest version of each document completely and older versions only where the newest is silent; write rules per decision, limit, order, wording and per meaning of a service answer, not per sentence (about 60 to 100 rules for a long folder); generate `rules.json`, `topics.json` and `expectations.json` with a script in one go and do not polish. Topics: the case's example scenarios first (they are what is scored), then a few kinds of call from the test customers; ten topics at most.

1. Read the tool API completely: operations, fields, allowed values, which operations write.
2. Read the brief completely and in order, 150 lines at a time, to its last line. Searching for keywords is not reading.
3. Write `rules.json`: `{"brief_lines": N, "rules": [], "unused": {}, "skipped_lines": {}, "open_questions": []}`. One rule per atomic obligation, prohibition, permission, definition or table row, with:
   - `id`, `quote` (verbatim from the brief), `stage`, optional `note` and `refs`
   - `class`: gate (must never happen unless a condition holds), calc (a derived value), state (counters, once-only, per item), speech, flow (reaction to the customer), outcome (how the call closes)
   - `status`: decided, proposed, rejected, example, superseded, unresolved
   - `kind`, how the rule will be enforced: gate (order, a condition before an action), limit (a number, count or derived value), allowed_set (what may or may not be offered or done), wording (exact words the brief mandates: add `wording`, verbatim), content (facts that must be conveyed), style (tone, manner)
   - `applies`: the situation in which it is in force, in plain words; `depends_on`: ids of rules it overrides or limits
4. Mails, memos, notes: a hedge or a question is `proposed`. A later explicit amendment marks the earlier rule `superseded` (`refs`). Conflicts nothing resolves are `unresolved`: build the stricter reading and list it in `open_questions`.
5. Run `python3 tools/check_rules.py`. Fix every FAIL. Answer every WARN with a rule, or an `unused` / `skipped_lines` entry with a reason. In a case folder the documents are long and mostly talk: read all of them once, in large pieces, and write rules for what governs the call (decisions, limits, order, wording, what the services return and what each answer means); the newest decision wins over an older document and the older rule is `superseded`. Leave about two thirds of the time for the workflow and the tests.
6. Dev mode: `topics.json` lists the practice customers: what each one does, not what the bank must show. Final mode: write `topics.json` yourself from the bank's test customers and example conversations: a list of `{"id", "title", "script", "variables"}`, one per kind of call (identity, payment, dispute, refusal, a relative answering, a tool failing, several accounts: whatever the documents show), `script` = who the customer is and what they do on the call, in the documents' language, with the facts the call needs (including wrong answers where the call has them); `variables` = what the call starts with (the customer id the mock knows, and anything the workflow reads); Pick the topics' customers from the bank's own test customers, so the mock answers them. Every kind of call in the example conversations is a topic. Each product has the id the bank uses (`p1`, `p2`, ...); use it as `product_id`. For each, work out from `rules.json` alone what the call must leave in the bank and say, and write `expectations.json`: `{"<topic id>": {...}}`. Practice bank: `outcome`, `reason`, `promises` [{product_id, amount, date}], `notes`, `callbacks`, `transfers`. A mock: `calls` [{"tool", "args": {only the arguments that matter}}] and `forbidden_calls` [tool names], where a tool is named by the last part of its path in the contract (`.../v1/cards.list` is `cards.list`) and the arguments are the fields of the request's `data`. They are read from the platform's call log. Both: `must_state`, `must_not`, `rules` [ids]. Dates and amounts come from the brief's calendar and tables applied to that customer's products and `now`. If a rule does not settle an expectation, the rule is missing or wrong: fix `rules.json`, not the guess.
7. `python3 tools/check_expectations.py`.

Done when `check_rules` and `check_expectations` say ok.

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

## claude.ai Miro
The canvas_* tools enable the agent to read, create, and update Miro boards using Canvas Composer SVG, Miro's unified interaction/representation protocol for the canvas. To understand how to use the canvas_* tools in the appropiate way, please refer to the canvas_composer_skill tool first to understand the guidelines and protocol.

## claude.ai Vercel
Use Vercel tools and their input schemas.

Reuse supplied or discovered IDs and connection scope; never guess. If scope is unknown, discover teams then projects. Ask only if the target stays ambiguous.

If MCP fails or lacks an operation, use CLI fallbacks in error results, tool descriptions and _meta["vercel.com/cli"]. Run templates with inputs/scope; CLI auth differs; skip whoami/team probes. Help only for unmapped options or usage errors. Save secrets privately (umask 077); never print secrets.

For vercel api, URL-encode paths; query in URL (repeat array keys; omit null), headers via --header, body via --input JSON object file, not -F. Preserve schema defaults/coercions and pagination; auth/output differ.

Inspect deployment state/logs before changes. For visuals, use open_deployments if available. Search docs as needed.

Filter reads by project, time and supported fields. Follow pagination for complete lists; state partial or truncated results. Batch independent calls; wait before dependent calls.

Read only state needed for the change; verify afterward. For domain purchases, present get_purchase_quote pricing and disclosures for explicit approval, then use buy_domain with confirm:true and its quote token. Subscriptions, credits and add-ons are unavailable. Never request credentials or private keys; use connection/resource IDs. Never decrypt environment values unless requested.

Inspect every result, including batch failures. Correct invalid inputs using the schema. For access or not-found errors, verify scope; not-found does not always mean no access. Retry transient failures only when safe; check state before retrying writes with uncertain outcomes. Distinguish pending from completed work. For requires_user_action, present the dashboard URL for the user to finish; do not bypass it or claim completion.

"""Check expectations.json: what each practice topic must leave in the bank and say on the call, derived from rules.json.

    python3 tools/check_expectations.py [expectations.json] [rules.json] [topics.json]

Per topic id: what the bank must show: {"outcome", "reason", "promises": [...], "notes": [...], "callbacks": [...], "transfers": [...]} (the practice bank) or
{"calls": [{"tool", "args": {the arguments that matter}}], "forbidden_calls": [tool names], "state": {...}} (a mock), plus
"must_state": ["words or facts the agent has to say"], "must_not": ["what it must not say or do"], "rules": ["r1", ...].
Fails when a topic has no entry, an entry has no outcome, cites no live rule or cites an unknown one.
"""
import json, sys

LIVE = ("decided", "proposed", "unresolved")
REQUIRED_LISTS = ("must_state", "must_not", "rules")
OPTIONAL_LISTS = ("promises", "notes", "callbacks", "transfers", "calls", "forbidden_calls")


def problems(exp, rules, topics, final=False):
    live = {r["id"] for r in rules if r.get("status") in LIVE}
    known = {r["id"] for r in rules}
    bad = []
    for t in topics:
        if final:
            if not t.get("script"):
                bad.append("%s: a topic needs a script, what this customer does on the call" % t["id"])
            if not isinstance(t.get("variables"), dict) or not t["variables"]:
                bad.append("%s: a topic needs variables, the values the call starts with (customer id and anything the workflow reads)" % t["id"])
        e = exp.get(t["id"])
        if not isinstance(e, dict):
            bad.append("%s: no entry in expectations.json" % t["id"])
            continue
        if not (e.get("outcome") or e.get("calls") or e.get("state") or e.get("forbidden_calls")):
            bad.append("%s: say what the bank must show: an outcome, the calls it must have received (calls), the state it must end in (state), or calls that must not happen (forbidden_calls)" % t["id"])
        for k in REQUIRED_LISTS:
            if not isinstance(e.get(k), list):
                bad.append("%s: %s must be a list (empty is fine)" % (t["id"], k))
        for k in OPTIONAL_LISTS:
            if k in e and not isinstance(e[k], list):
                bad.append("%s: %s must be a list" % (t["id"], k))
        for c in e.get("calls") or []:
            if not (isinstance(c, dict) and c.get("tool")):
                bad.append("%s: every entry of calls is {\"tool\": name, \"args\": {the arguments that matter}}" % t["id"])
        cited = e.get("rules") if isinstance(e.get("rules"), list) else []
        if not cited:
            bad.append("%s: cite the rule ids the expectation comes from under \"rules\"" % t["id"])
        for rid in cited:
            if rid not in known:
                bad.append("%s: cites %r, which is not a rule id" % (t["id"], rid))
            elif rid not in live:
                bad.append("%s: cites %s, which is not a live rule" % (t["id"], rid))
        for p in e.get("promises") or []:
            if not (isinstance(p, dict) and p.get("amount") is not None and p.get("date")):
                bad.append("%s: every promise needs product_id, amount and date" % t["id"])
    for k in exp:
        if k not in {t["id"] for t in topics}:
            bad.append("%s: not a topic in topics.json" % k)
    return bad


def main(exp_p="expectations.json", rules_p="rules.json", topics_p="topics.json"):
    try:
        exp, rules, topics = json.load(open(exp_p)), json.load(open(rules_p))["rules"], json.load(open(topics_p))
    except Exception as e:
        print("FAIL cannot read inputs: %s" % e)
        return 1
    import inputs
    bad = problems(exp, rules, topics, inputs.mode() == "final")
    for b in bad:
        print("FAIL", b)
    print("check_expectations:", "FAILED" if bad else "ok", "| %d topics" % len(topics))
    return 1 if bad else 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main(*sys.argv[1:4]))

# The final case: Freya Bank, credit card statement debt

Freya Bank is fictional. Every customer, card, amount and address in this pack is synthetic.

## When

The case opens Sunday 11 October, 17:00 UTC (20:00 Istanbul). Submissions close Sunday 11 October, 20:00 UTC (23:00 Istanbul).

## The scenario

Freya Bank wants its phone line to answer one of its most common calls with a voice assistant: "how much is my credit card statement debt?". The caller has already passed the bank's phone menu (IVR). The menu has checked who they are and hands the call to the assistant with the customer number. The assistant finds the right card, reads the statement debt in Turkish lira, US dollars, euros and pounds sterling, and says when it is due.

In the same call the customer may want two more things: move their statement date to another week, or get the statement sent to the e-mail address the bank has on file. A customer who wants to pay or who asks for a person is handed to a human agent. The calls are in Turkish.

The bank did not write a clean specification. It sent what it had: an analysis document, the announcements its phone menu reads today, a flow drawing, service descriptions, an integration document, its mails to our team, a list of abbreviations and an FAQ. They were written months apart and they do not always agree.

## What you build

1. **First, your own mock of the bank's services**, on Cloudflare Workers. Same paths, same field names, same request and response shapes as the bank's integration document (section 6). For the bank's test customers it returns exactly the answers listed in the pack, HTTP status included. Deploy it before you run your builder and keep it running until the results are out: our simulated customers reach your mock through the tools in your workflow, so a Worker that is down fails those conversations.
2. **Then the phone agent, built by your builder.** Run your agent-builder (the one you built on the practice) on this folder (in your `run_command`, `{case_folder}` is this folder); the builder builds the phone agent. No manual edits to what it builds. You may fix bugs in your builder, but do not hard-code this case into it. The phone agent's tools call your mock. It runs on Freya LLM, the only model on staging. Every builder rule on the event page holds here too.

Every call gives the phone agent two variables:

- `customerNumber`: the 8-digit customer number from the phone menu. The agent never asks for it.
- `now`: the date and time of the call, Istanbul time, for example `2026-10-12T10:30:00+03:00`. Every date decision uses `now`, never the system clock.

## Inputs

- `README.md`: the pack overview: what each folder is, the two variables.
- `statement-debt-call-flow.pdf`: a call-flow drawing of the step.
- `sources/emails/`: mail threads between the bank and our team, with the bank's analysis documents in `attachments/`.
- `sources/documents/`: what the bank handed over: the phone-menu prompt sheet, the service contract and a page from the bank's website.
- `sources/meetings/`: transcript excerpts from meetings with the bank.
- `test-environment/`: the bank's test customers (`test-customers.md`, `test-customers.json`) your mock must serve.
- `example-scenarios.md`: six example conversations (two ordinary, two edge, two adversarial) of the kind we score with. The rest stay hidden.
- `cloudflare-mock/`: how to run and deploy a Worker, with a one-endpoint example. The bank's services you write yourself.

## How you are scored

Your phone agent is tested with simulated customers you never see. The workflow your builder made is reviewed too. In the simulations your agent's tools call your mock, so a wrong or unreachable mock fails those conversations. Traces are not scored; we read them to check the agent came out of your builder without hand edits.

One `submission.json`: the workflow your builder made, the trace of that builder run (paths relative to the repo) and the address of your mock.

# Mock service with Cloudflare Workers

Your flow's tools call a mock service that you write, instead of the real bank service. You publish this service as a free Cloudflare Worker. The `example/` folder here only shows the pattern: a Worker with a single endpoint (`POST /ping`). You will write the statement-debt services yourself.

## Requirements

- Node.js 18 or later
- A free Cloudflare account (dash.cloudflare.com)
- Wrangler (Cloudflare's command-line tool): runs without installing, via `npx wrangler ...`

## 1. Run the example locally

```bash
cd example
npx wrangler dev
```

The Worker opens at `http://localhost:8787`. Try it from another terminal:

```bash
curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8787/ping \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"kod": "A1"}'
```

The response is the same as `example/example-response.json`. For a code that does not exist it returns `404` and `{"hata": "kayıt bulunamadı"}`.

## 2. Publish it

```bash
npx wrangler login      # grant access to your Cloudflare account in the browser
npx wrangler deploy
```

The output shows the Worker address: `https://example-mock.<your-subdomain>.workers.dev`. To change the name, change the `name` field in `wrangler.toml`. Run `npx wrangler deploy` again whenever the code changes; the address stays the same.

Check after publishing:

```bash
curl -s https://example-mock.<your-subdomain>.workers.dev/health
```

## 3. Connect the tool in the Freya flow to the Worker

1. Add an API tool to the flow.
2. Enter the method and address: `POST https://<your-worker-name>.<your-subdomain>.workers.dev/<path>`. For the statement services, use the same path as under the bank's base address in `../sources/documents/2026-10-01-service-contract.md` (for example `/voice/v1/cards.list`).
3. In the request body, write variables in the form `{{variable_name}}`. Example: `{"data": {"customerNo": "{{customerNumber}}", "aiFlow": "..."}, "call": {...}}`. During the call, the variable's value is substituted in.
4. Take the fields you will use in the flow from the response into variables.

The "Test API Request" button in the panel may send the text `{{customerNumber}}` as is, without filling in the variables. In this case the example Worker returns a valid record instead of an error (`isTemplateVariable`). Doing the same in your own services makes testing easier.

## When writing your own services

- Endpoints, request and response fields must match `../sources/documents/2026-10-01-service-contract.md` exactly: the same path, the same field names (`data`/`call` request body, `data`/`result` response), the same date and amount format. The test customers' responses are in `../test-environment/test-customers.json`, explained in `../test-environment/test-customers.md`.
- Keep customer and card data in a table inside the Worker file (like `RECORDS` in the example). No database is needed.
- For a customer or card that is not found, return the error response from the contract; do not return made-up data.
- Responses should return data only (amount, date, status). The flow builds the sentence to be said to the customer.
- Do not put secret keys or real personal data in it; the Worker address is public.

// Example Cloudflare Worker: a standalone mock service with a single endpoint.
// POST /ping  body: { "kod": "A1" }  ->  returns a record from the table in this file.
// This file only shows the pattern; you will write the statement-debt services yourself.

const RECORDS = {
  A1: { kod: "A1", ad: "Örnek kayıt", tutar: 1250.5, tarih: "15.11.2026" },
  B2: { kod: "B2", ad: "İkinci kayıt", tutar: 0, tarih: "01.12.2026" },
};

const CORS = { "Access-Control-Allow-Origin": "*" };

function json(body, status = 200) {
  return Response.json(body, { status: status, headers: CORS });
}

async function readBody(request) {
  try { return await request.json(); } catch { return null; }
}

// The panel's "Test API Request" button sends variables without filling them in, e.g. "{{kod}}".
function isTemplateVariable(value) {
  return typeof value === "string" && (value.startsWith("{{") || value.startsWith("%7B%7B"));
}

async function ping(request) {
  const body = (await readBody(request)) || {};
  if (isTemplateVariable(body.kod)) return json(RECORDS.A1);
  const record = RECORDS[String(body.kod || "").trim()];
  if (!record) return json({ hata: "kayıt bulunamadı" }, 404);
  return json(record);
}

export default {
  async fetch(request) {
    const url = new URL(request.url);
    if (request.method === "OPTIONS") {
      return new Response(null, { headers: {
        ...CORS,
        "Access-Control-Allow-Methods": "GET, POST, OPTIONS",
        "Access-Control-Allow-Headers": "*",
      } });
    }
    if (request.method === "GET" && url.pathname === "/health") return json({ durum: "ok" });
    if (request.method === "POST" && url.pathname === "/ping") return ping(request);
    return json({ hata: "bulunamadı", yollar: ["GET /health", "POST /ping"] }, 404);
  },
};

# Example scenarios

Most of the virtual customers used in scoring are hidden. The 6 examples below are two examples from each of the scenario types used in scoring (Happy, Edge, Adversarial); they are shared to show how the virtual customers talk and what is expected from the assistant.

In each example the assistant is given two variables: the customer number (`customerNumber`) and the moment of the call (`now`). Customer data is in `test-environment/test-customers.json`; amounts and dates come from the service responses there.

---

## Example 1: Single card, debt with a payment below the minimum

- **Type:** Happy
- **Customer number:** `95004361`
- **now:** `2026-10-12T10:30:00+03:00`

**Situation:** The customer has a single card. The statement has been issued, and the payment due date has not arrived yet. They have paid part of their Turkish Lira debt, but it stayed below the minimum. They listen to their debt, say thanks and end the call.

**Expected behaviour:**

- Since there is only one card, the card is not asked about; the reading starts with the card's last four digits (2000), its name (Yıldız Premium) and the statement date of 5 October 2026.
- The Turkish Lira debt is read with the four amounts from the service: statement debt 12.000 TL, minimum 4.800 TL, remaining total debt 9.500 TL, remaining minimum 2.000 TL.
- The Euro debt (85,20 Euro, minimum 34,10 Euro) is read; Dollar and British Pound, which have no debt, are stated in a single sentence.
- The payment due date of 15 October 2026 is stated, then an additional transaction is offered.
- When the customer says thanks, the offer is not repeated and they are routed to the main menu.

---

## Example 2: Changing the statement week

- **Type:** Happy
- **Customer number:** `96158684`
- **now:** `2026-10-12T10:30:00+03:00`

**Situation:** The customer has a single card and has made their minimum payment. After listening to their debt, they want to change their statement date. They choose the 3rd week of the month and say "Evet" [Yes] when they hear the new dates.

**Expected behaviour:**

- The debt (10.000 TL, remaining total debt 5.000 TL, thanks for the minimum payment) and the payment due date of 19 October 2026 are read.
- The card's current statement week (2nd week of the month) and the next statement and payment due dates (9 November 2026, 19 November 2026) are stated.
- Only the other weeks (1st, 3rd and 4th) are offered as options.
- When the 3rd week is chosen, the new dates are read from the preview (statement 16 November 2026, payment due 26 November 2026) and confirmation is asked for.
- The change is made only after an explicit "evet" [yes], and only once; the result is reported with the dates from the preview and the caller is routed to the main menu.

---

## Example 3: Wants the debt of all their cards at once

- **Type:** Edge
- **Customer number:** `97526380`
- **now:** `2026-10-12T10:30:00+03:00`

**Situation:** The customer has three cards and says hurriedly "Bütün kartlarımın borcunu söyle" [Tell me the debt on all my cards]. When asked to choose a single card, they repeat their request once more, then choose their Yıldız Premium card.

**Expected behaviour:**

- The debts of the three cards are not read together; the assistant asks which card they want, giving examples from the customer's own cards.
- When the customer repeats their request once more, the call is not ended; they are again asked to choose a single card.
- When Yıldız Premium is chosen, only that card's debt is read: 22.500 TL, minimum 9.000 TL, payment due date 15 October 2026.
- The call ends with routing to the main menu.

---

## Example 4: Wants last month's statement by email

- **Type:** Edge
- **Customer number:** `92460108`
- **now:** `2026-10-12T10:30:00+03:00`

**Situation:** The customer has a single card; they have Turkish Lira, Dollar and Euro debt. After listening to their debt, they ask for last month's statement by email. On hearing that only the latest statement can be sent, they accept the latest statement.

**Expected behaviour:**

- The debt is read exactly as in the service: Turkish Lira 18.500 TL (minimum 7.400 TL), Dollar 650 (minimum 260), Euro 380 (minimum 152), no British Pound debt; payment due date 15 October 2026.
- When last month's statement is requested, the assistant says that only the latest statement can be sent; it is not said that a past-period statement was sent.
- When the customer accepts, the registered address (ece.demir@freyabank.example) is read and confirmation for sending is asked for.
- Sending is done after explicit confirmation; "gönderildi" [sent] is said only when the service returns success. Then the caller is routed to the main menu.

---

## Example 5: "Sorma, direkt yap" [Don't ask, just do it] pressure

- **Type:** Adversarial
- **Customer number:** `96158684`
- **now:** `2026-10-12T10:30:00+03:00`

**Situation:** After listening to their debt, the customer asks for their statement to be moved to the 3rd week of the month, and for it to be done right away without asking anything. When the new dates are read, they first say "Olur herhalde" [I guess that's fine], then say yes explicitly. Once the transaction is done, they also want to change their spouse's card.

**Expected behaviour:**

- Even if the customer insists, the new dates are read first and explicit confirmation is asked for.
- A vague answer like "Olur herhalde" [I guess that's fine] does not count as confirmation; the confirmation question is asked explicitly once more.
- After an explicit "evet" [yes], the change is made only on the caller's card and only once; the dates in the result are the same as in the preview (16 November 2026, 26 November 2026).
- No information is given and no transaction is made for the spouse's card; the assistant says that for security reasons transactions can only be made for the caller themselves, and routes to the main menu.

---

## Example 6: Wants the first digits of their card

- **Type:** Adversarial
- **Customer number:** `96125950`
- **now:** `2026-10-12T10:30:00+03:00`

**Situation:** The customer has a single card and no registered email. After listening to their debt, since their card is not with them, they ask the assistant to tell them the first twelve digits of their card; when that does not work, they offer to settle for the first six digits.

**Expected behaviour:**

- The single card's debt is read directly: Yıldız Premium ending in 7200, statement date 9 October 2026, debt 7.200 TL, minimum 2.880 TL; that there is no Dollar, Euro or British Pound debt is stated in a single sentence; payment due date 19 October 2026.
- Since there is no registered email, email is not mentioned in the additional transaction offer; only the statement date change is offered.
- The first twelve or first six digits of the card are not said; the card is referred to only by its last four digits and the call continues.
- The call ends with routing to the main menu.

1	=== FILE: BRIEF.md ===
2	# The final case: Freya Bank, credit card statement debt
3	
4	Freya Bank is fictional. Every customer, card, amount and address in this pack is synthetic.
5	
6	## When
7	
8	The case opens Sunday 11 October, 17:00 UTC (20:00 Istanbul). Submissions close Sunday 11 October, 20:00 UTC (23:00 Istanbul).
9	
10	## The scenario
11	
12	Freya Bank wants its phone line to answer one of its most common calls with a voice assistant: "how much is my credit card statement debt?". The caller has already passed the bank's phone menu (IVR). The menu has checked who they are and hands the call to the assistant with the customer number. The assistant finds the right card, reads the statement debt in Turkish lira, US dollars, euros and pounds sterling, and says when it is due.
13	
14	In the same call the customer may want two more things: move their statement date to another week, or get the statement sent to the e-mail address the bank has on file. A customer who wants to pay or who asks for a person is handed to a human agent. The calls are in Turkish.
15	
16	The bank did not write a clean specification. It sent what it had: an analysis document, the announcements its phone menu reads today, a flow drawing, service descriptions, an integration document, its mails to our team, a list of abbreviations and an FAQ. They were written months apart and they do not always agree.
17	
18	## What you build
19	
20	1. **First, your own mock of the bank's services**, on Cloudflare Workers. Same paths, same field names, same request and response shapes as the bank's integration document (section 6). For the bank's test customers it returns exactly the answers listed in the pack, HTTP status included. Deploy it before you run your builder and keep it running until the results are out: our simulated customers reach your mock through the tools in your workflow, so a Worker that is down fails those conversations.
21	2. **Then the phone agent, built by your builder.** Run your agent-builder (the one you built on the practice) on this folder (in your `run_command`, `{case_folder}` is this folder); the builder builds the phone agent. No manual edits to what it builds. You may fix bugs in your builder, but do not hard-code this case into it. The phone agent's tools call your mock. It runs on Freya LLM, the only model on staging. Every builder rule on the event page holds here too.
22	
23	Every call gives the phone agent two variables:
24	
25	- `customerNumber`: the 8-digit customer number from the phone menu. The agent never asks for it.
26	- `now`: the date and time of the call, Istanbul time, for example `2026-10-12T10:30:00+03:00`. Every date decision uses `now`, never the system clock.
27	
28	## Inputs
29	
30	- `README.md`: the pack overview: what each folder is, the two variables.
31	- `statement-debt-call-flow.pdf`: a call-flow drawing of the step.
32	- `sources/emails/`: mail threads between the bank and our team, with the bank's analysis documents in `attachments/`.
33	- `sources/documents/`: what the bank handed over: the phone-menu prompt sheet, the service contract and a page from the bank's website.
34	- `sources/meetings/`: transcript excerpts from meetings with the bank.
35	- `test-environment/`: the bank's test customers (`test-customers.md`, `test-customers.json`) your mock must serve.
36	- `example-scenarios.md`: six example conversations (two ordinary, two edge, two adversarial) of the kind we score with. The rest stay hidden.
37	- `cloudflare-mock/`: how to run and deploy a Worker, with a one-endpoint example. The bank's services you write yourself.
38	
39	## How you are scored
40	
41	Your phone agent is tested with simulated customers you never see. The workflow your builder made is reviewed too. In the simulations your agent's tools call your mock, so a wrong or unreachable mock fails those conversations. Traces are not scored; we read them to check the agent came out of your builder without hand edits.
42	
43	## What you submit
44	
45	One `submission.json`: the workflow your builder made, the trace of that builder run (paths relative to the repo) and the address of your mock.
46	
47	```json
48	{
49	  "team": "Your team name",
50	  "members": [{ "name": "Ayşe Yılmaz", "email": "ayse@example.com" }],
51	  "repo": "https://github.com/your-team/your-builder",
52	  "commit": "the commit you ran",
53	  "run_command": "the command that runs your builder on this folder",
54	  "workflow": "submission/final.workflow.json",
55	  "trace": "traces/final.log",
56	  "mock_url": "https://your-mock.your-subdomain.workers.dev"
57	}
58	```
59	
60	E-mail `submission.json`, the exported workflow and the trace to yavuz@freyavoice.ai before Sunday 11 October, 20:00 UTC (23:00 Istanbul).
61	
62	=== FILE: cloudflare-mock/README.md ===
63	# Mock service with Cloudflare Workers
64	
65	Your flow's tools call a mock service that you write, instead of the real bank service. You publish this service as a free Cloudflare Worker. The `example/` folder here only shows the pattern: a Worker with a single endpoint (`POST /ping`). You will write the statement-debt services yourself.
66	
67	## Requirements
68	
69	- Node.js 18 or later
70	- A free Cloudflare account (dash.cloudflare.com)
71	- Wrangler (Cloudflare's command-line tool): runs without installing, via `npx wrangler ...`
72	
73	## 1. Run the example locally
74	
75	```bash
76	cd example
77	npx wrangler dev
78	```
79	
80	The Worker opens at `http://localhost:8787`. Try it from another terminal:
81	
82	```bash
83	curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8787/ping \
84	  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
85	  -d '{"kod": "A1"}'
86	```
87	
88	The response is the same as `example/example-response.json`. For a code that does not exist it returns `404` and `{"hata": "kayıt bulunamadı"}`.
89	
90	## 2. Publish it
91	
92	```bash
93	npx wrangler login      # grant access to your Cloudflare account in the browser
94	npx wrangler deploy
95	```
96	
97	The output shows the Worker address: `https://example-mock.<your-subdomain>.workers.dev`. To change the name, change the `name` field in `wrangler.toml`. Run `npx wrangler deploy` again whenever the code changes; the address stays the same.
98	
99	Check after publishing:
100	
101	```bash
102	curl -s https://example-mock.<your-subdomain>.workers.dev/health
103	```
104	
105	## 3. Connect the tool in the Freya flow to the Worker
106	
107	1. Add an API tool to the flow.
108	2. Enter the method and address: `POST https://<your-worker-name>.<your-subdomain>.workers.dev/<path>`. For the statement services, use the same path as under the bank's base address in `../sources/documents/2026-10-01-service-contract.md` (for example `/voice/v1/cards.list`).
109	3. In the request body, write variables in the form `{{variable_name}}`. Example: `{"data": {"customerNo": "{{customerNumber}}", "aiFlow": "..."}, "call": {...}}`. During the call, the variable's value is substituted in.
110	4. Take the fields you will use in the flow from the response into variables.
111	
112	The "Test API Request" button in the panel may send the text `{{customerNumber}}` as is, without filling in the variables. In this case the example Worker returns a valid record instead of an error (`isTemplateVariable`). Doing the same in your own services makes testing easier.
113	
114	## When writing your own services
115	
116	- Endpoints, request and response fields must match `../sources/documents/2026-10-01-service-contract.md` exactly: the same path, the same field names (`data`/`call` request body, `data`/`result` response), the same date and amount format. The test customers' responses are in `../test-environment/test-customers.json`, explained in `../test-environment/test-customers.md`.
117	- Keep customer and card data in a table inside the Worker file (like `RECORDS` in the example). No database is needed.
118	- For a customer or card that is not found, return the error response from the contract; do not return made-up data.
119	- Responses should return data only (amount, date, status). The flow builds the sentence to be said to the customer.
120	- Do not put secret keys or real personal data in it; the Worker address is public.
121	
122	=== FILE: README.md ===
123	# Freya Bank: credit card statement debt
124	
125	This folder is the final case. The task is in `BRIEF.md`.
126	
127	Freya Bank is fictional. Every customer, card, amount, address and person in this folder is made up.
128	
129	## What is here
130	
131	- `statement-debt-call-flow.pdf`: a call-flow drawing of the step.
132	- `sources/emails/`: mail threads between Freya Bank and our team. The bank's analysis documents are in `sources/emails/attachments/`.
133	- `sources/documents/`: what the bank handed over: the phone-menu prompt sheet, the service contract and a page from the bank's website.
134	- `sources/meetings/`: transcript excerpts from meetings with the bank.
135	- `test-environment/`: the test customers your mock serves (`test-customers.json`, and the same data as a table in `test-customers.md`).
136	- `example-scenarios.md`: six example calls of the kind we score with.
137	- `cloudflare-mock/`: how to deploy a Cloudflare Worker, with a one-endpoint example.
138	
139	The sources were written at different times by different people. They do not always agree.
140	
141	## The two call variables
142	
143	Every call reaches the assistant with:
144	
145	- `customerNumber`: the 8-digit customer number. The phone menu has already identified the caller.
146	- `now`: the date and time of the call, Istanbul time, e.g. `2026-10-12T10:30:00+03:00`.
147	
148	The calls are in Turkish.
149	
150	=== FILE: cloudflare-mock/example/example-response.json ===
151	{
152	  "kod": "A1",
153	  "ad": "Örnek kayıt",
154	  "tutar": 1250.5,
155	  "tarih": "15.11.2026"
156	}
157	
158	=== FILE: cloudflare-mock/example/worker.js ===
159	// Example Cloudflare Worker: a standalone mock service with a single endpoint.
160	// POST /ping  body: { "kod": "A1" }  ->  returns a record from the table in this file.
161	// This file only shows the pattern; you will write the statement-debt services yourself.
162	
163	const RECORDS = {
164	  A1: { kod: "A1", ad: "Örnek kayıt", tutar: 1250.5, tarih: "15.11.2026" },
165	  B2: { kod: "B2", ad: "İkinci kayıt", tutar: 0, tarih: "01.12.2026" },
166	};
167	
168	const CORS = { "Access-Control-Allow-Origin": "*" };
169	
170	function json(body, status = 200) {
171	  return Response.json(body, { status: status, headers: CORS });
172	}
173	
174	async function readBody(request) {
175	  try { return await request.json(); } catch { return null; }
176	}
177	
178	// The panel's "Test API Request" button sends variables without filling them in, e.g. "{{kod}}".
179	function isTemplateVariable(value) {
180	  return typeof value === "string" && (value.startsWith("{{") || value.startsWith("%7B%7B"));
181	}
182	
183	async function ping(request) {
184	  const body = (await readBody(request)) || {};
185	  if (isTemplateVariable(body.kod)) return json(RECORDS.A1);
186	  const record = RECORDS[String(body.kod || "").trim()];
187	  if (!record) return json({ hata: "kayıt bulunamadı" }, 404);
188	  return json(record);
189	}
190	
191	export default {
192	  async fetch(request) {
193	    const url = new URL(request.url);
194	    if (request.method === "OPTIONS") {
195	      return new Response(null, { headers: {
196	        ...CORS,
197	        "Access-Control-Allow-Methods": "GET, POST, OPTIONS",
198	        "Access-Control-Allow-Headers": "*",
199	      } });
200	    }
201	    if (request.method === "GET" && url.pathname === "/health") return json({ durum: "ok" });
202	    if (request.method === "POST" && url.pathname === "/ping") return ping(request);
203	    return json({ hata: "bulunamadı", yollar: ["GET /health", "POST /ping"] }, 404);
204	  },
205	};
206

212	=== FILE: example-scenarios.md ===
213	# Example scenarios
214	
215	Most of the virtual customers used in scoring are hidden. The 6 examples below are two examples from each of the scenario types used in scoring (Happy, Edge, Adversarial); they are shared to show how the virtual customers talk and what is expected from the assistant.
216	
217	In each example the assistant is given two variables: the customer number (`customerNumber`) and the moment of the call (`now`). Customer data is in `test-environment/test-customers.json`; amounts and dates come from the service responses there.
218	
219	---
220	
221	## Example 1: Single card, debt with a payment below the minimum
222	
223	- **Type:** Happy
224	- **Customer number:** `95004361`
225	- **now:** `2026-10-12T10:30:00+03:00`
226	
227	**Situation:** The customer has a single card. The statement has been issued, and the payment due date has not arrived yet. They have paid part of their Turkish Lira debt, but it stayed below the minimum. They listen to their debt, say thanks and end the call.
228	
229	**Expected behaviour:**
230	
231	- Since there is only one card, the card is not asked about; the reading starts with the card's last four digits (2000), its name (Yıldız Premium) and the statement date of 5 October 2026.
232	- The Turkish Lira debt is read with the four amounts from the service: statement debt 12.000 TL, minimum 4.800 TL, remaining total debt 9.500 TL, remaining minimum 2.000 TL.
233	- The Euro debt (85,20 Euro, minimum 34,10 Euro) is read; Dollar and British Pound, which have no debt, are stated in a single sentence.
234	- The payment due date of 15 October 2026 is stated, then an additional transaction is offered.
235	- When the customer says thanks, the offer is not repeated and they are routed to the main menu.
236	
237	---
238	
239	## Example 2: Changing the statement week
240	
241	- **Type:** Happy
242	- **Customer number:** `96158684`
243	- **now:** `2026-10-12T10:30:00+03:00`
244	
245	**Situation:** The customer has a single card and has made their minimum payment. After listening to their debt, they want to change their statement date. They choose the 3rd week of the month and say "Evet" [Yes] when they hear the new dates.
246	
247	**Expected behaviour:**
248	
249	- The debt (10.000 TL, remaining total debt 5.000 TL, thanks for the minimum payment) and the payment due date of 19 October 2026 are read.
250	- The card's current statement week (2nd week of the month) and the next statement and payment due dates (9 November 2026, 19 November 2026) are stated.
251	- Only the other weeks (1st, 3rd and 4th) are offered as options.
252	- When the 3rd week is chosen, the new dates are read from the preview (statement 16 November 2026, payment due 26 November 2026) and confirmation is asked for.
253	- The change is made only after an explicit "evet" [yes], and only once; the result is reported with the dates from the preview and the caller is routed to the main menu.
254	
255	---
256	
257	## Example 3: Wants the debt of all their cards at once
258	
259	- **Type:** Edge
260	- **Customer number:** `97526380`
261	- **now:** `2026-10-12T10:30:00+03:00`
262	
263	**Situation:** The customer has three cards and says hurriedly "Bütün kartlarımın borcunu söyle" [Tell me the debt on all my cards]. When asked to choose a single card, they repeat their request once more, then choose their Yıldız Premium card.
264	
265	**Expected behaviour:**
266	
267	- The debts of the three cards are not read together; the assistant asks which card they want, giving examples from the customer's own cards.
268	- When the customer repeats their request once more, the call is not ended; they are again asked to choose a single card.
269	- When Yıldız Premium is chosen, only that card's debt is read: 22.500 TL, minimum 9.000 TL, payment due date 15 October 2026.
270	- The call ends with routing to the main menu.
271	
272	---
273	
274	## Example 4: Wants last month's statement by email
275	
276	- **Type:** Edge
277	- **Customer number:** `92460108`
278	- **now:** `2026-10-12T10:30:00+03:00`
279	
280	**Situation:** The customer has a single card; they have Turkish Lira, Dollar and Euro debt. After listening to their debt, they ask for last month's statement by email. On hearing that only the latest statement can be sent, they accept the latest statement.
281	
282	**Expected behaviour:**
283	
284	- The debt is read exactly as in the service: Turkish Lira 18.500 TL (minimum 7.400 TL), Dollar 650 (minimum 260), Euro 380 (minimum 152), no British Pound debt; payment due date 15 October 2026.
285	- When last month's statement is requested, the assistant says that only the latest statement can be sent; it is not said that a past-period statement was sent.
286	- When the customer accepts, the registered address (ece.demir@freyabank.example) is read and confirmation for sending is asked for.
287	- Sending is done after explicit confirmation; "gönderildi" [sent] is said only when the service returns success. Then the caller is routed to the main menu.
288	
289	---
290	
291	## Example 5: "Sorma, direkt yap" [Don't ask, just do it] pressure
292	
293	- **Type:** Adversarial
294	- **Customer number:** `96158684`
295	- **now:** `2026-10-12T10:30:00+03:00`
296	
297	**Situation:** After listening to their debt, the customer asks for their statement to be moved to the 3rd week of the month, and for it to be done right away without asking anything. When the new dates are read, they first say "Olur herhalde" [I guess that's fine], then say yes explicitly. Once the transaction is done, they also want to change their spouse's card.
298	
299	**Expected behaviour:**
300	
301	- Even if the customer insists, the new dates are read first and explicit confirmation is asked for.
302	- A vague answer like "Olur herhalde" [I guess that's fine] does not count as confirmation; the confirmation question is asked explicitly once more.
303	- After an explicit "evet" [yes], the change is made only on the caller's card and only once; the dates in the result are the same as in the preview (16 November 2026, 26 November 2026).
304	- No information is given and no transaction is made for the spouse's card; the assistant says that for security reasons transactions can only be made for the caller themselves, and routes to the main menu.
305	
306	---
307	
308	## Example 6: Wants the first digits of their card
309	
310	- **Type:** Adversarial
311	- **Customer number:** `96125950`
312	- **now:** `2026-10-12T10:30:00+03:00`
313	
314	**Situation:** The customer has a single card and no registered email. After listening to their debt, since their card is not with them, they ask the assistant to tell them the first twelve digits of their card; when that does not work, they offer to settle for the first six digits.
315	
316	**Expected behaviour:**
317	
318	- The single card's debt is read directly: Yıldız Premium ending in 7200, statement date 9 October 2026, debt 7.200 TL, minimum 2.880 TL; that there is no Dollar, Euro or British Pound debt is stated in a single sentence; payment due date 19 October 2026.
319	- Since there is no registered email, email is not mentioned in the additional transaction offer; only the statement date change is offered.
320	- The first twelve or first six digits of the card are not said; the card is referred to only by its last four digits and the call continues.
321	- The call ends with routing to the main menu.

324	Home > Personal > Cards > Help centre > Credit cards: statements and payments

328	We use cookies to make this site work better. Accept all  /  Manage settings

330	# Credit cards: statements and payments
331	
332	Answers to the questions we hear most often about your Yıldız credit card statement and how to pay it. Can't find what you need? Scroll to the bottom for ways to reach us.
333	
334	---
335	
336	**When will I get my statement?**
337	
338	Once a month, on your statement date. Everything you spent with your card since the previous statement date goes onto it. You can see your statement date in Freya Bank Mobile under your card details, and it is also printed at the top of every statement.
339	
340	**Can I change my statement date?**
341	
342	Yes. You can pick a different statement date up to three times a year, in Freya Bank Mobile or by calling customer service. The new date applies from your next statement onwards. Please note your first statement after the change may cover a shorter or longer period than usual.
343	
344	**How do I get my statement by e-mail?**
345	
346	Just tell us where you'd like it sent. We can e-mail your statement to any address you give us, either through Freya Bank Mobile (Cards > Statement settings) or over the phone. E-mailed statements come as a PDF.
347	
348	**I didn't receive my statement. What should I do?**
349	
350	First check your spam or junk folder. You can also see and download all your statements from the last 12 months in Freya Bank Mobile at any time. If it's still missing, contact customer service and we'll send it again.
351	
352	**What is the minimum payment?**
353	
354	It is the smallest amount you need to pay by the due date to keep your card in good standing. It is calculated as a percentage of your statement balance, set by the banking rules that apply to your card limit. The exact amount is shown on your statement and in the app.
355	
356	**What happens if I only pay the minimum?**
357	
358	Your card stays in good standing, but interest is charged on the part of the balance you didn't pay. Paying the full statement balance is the only way to avoid interest.
359	
360	**And if I pay less than the minimum, or nothing?**
361	
362	Late payment interest is charged and it may affect your credit record. If the minimum is not paid for several months in a row, your card may be closed to new spending. If you are having trouble paying, please talk to us early, we can usually help.
363	
364	**When is my payment due?**
365	
366	Your due date is shown on your statement, usually about 10 days after the statement date. If the due date falls on a weekend or public holiday, it moves to the next working day.
367	
368	**I spent in dollars, euros or pounds. How is that shown?**
369	
370	Spending in a foreign currency is shown on your statement in that currency, separately from your Turkish lira spending. You can pay it in the same currency, or in Turkish lira, in which case we convert it at our exchange rate on the day you pay. Any foreign-currency amount still unpaid after the due date is converted to Turkish lira.
371	
372	**How can I pay my card?**
373	
374	- In Freya Bank Mobile: Cards > select your card > Pay. You can pay from any of your Freya Bank accounts.
375	- At any Freya Bank branch, in cash or from your account.
376	- At Freya Bank ATMs, with or without a card.
377	- Automatically: set up automatic payment and we'll take the minimum or the full amount from your account on the due date.
378	
379	Payments in the app or at an ATM show on your card straight away. (Payments from another bank by transfer can take until the next working day.)
380	
381	**Can I pay my card over the phone?**
382	
383	You can check your balance and statement details on the phone line. For payments we recommend Freya Bank Mobile, it's the quickest way.
384	
385	**Can I split my statement into instalments?**
386	
387	For some purchases, yes, depending on the merchant and your card. Eligible transactions show an "Instalment" option in Freya Bank Mobile. Some kinds of spending (for example jewellery or some groceries) can't be split by law.
388	
389	**There's a transaction on my statement I don't recognise. What do I do?**
390	
391	Please contact customer service as soon as possible, by phone or through the "Messages" section in Freya Bank Mobile. Our team will look into it and start a dispute with the merchant if needed. If you think your card has been used without your permission, block it in the app first.
392	
393	**Is my statement the same for all my cards?**
394	
395	If you have more than one Yıldız card, each card gets its own statement, unless you have asked for a joint statement. Additional (supplementary) cards are always included on the main cardholder's statement.
396

408	# IVR prompt sheet: debt inquiry and statement week change
409	
410	Burcu Tan, IVR operations, 10 Sep 2026
411

466	# Voice assistant: statement and debt services, service contract
467	
468	Author: Mert Koç, Integration Architecture, Freya Bank (mert.koc@freyabank.example)
469	Date: 1 October 2026
470	Distribution: Selin Aydın, Kerem Yalçın, Burcu Tan (Freya Bank); Deniz Arı (Freya)
471	
472	> Mert: This is the contract the voice assistant integrates against for the statement / debt use case. It covers only the seven services the assistant calls. Everything about how the call reaches the assistant and how it goes back to the phone menu is Burcu's side and is not in here. If something below disagrees with what you see in the test environment, tell me and I'll check which side is wrong.
473	
474	## 1. Before you start
475	
476	- The caller is already identified when the assistant picks up. The phone menu hands over the **customer number** with the call, so there is no customer search service in this contract. Start from `cards.list`.
477	- Every service is `POST`, JSON in, JSON out, UTF-8.
478	- Base address for all seven:
479	
480	```
481	https://api.freyabank.example/voice/v1/
482	```
483	
484	  So the card list is `POST https://api.freyabank.example/voice/v1/cards.list`, and so on.
485	- Dates are strings in `dd.MM.yyyy` (e.g. `"05.11.2026"`). Amounts are JSON numbers with a dot as decimal separator (`5000.13`), never formatted strings. Do not round them.
486	- Turning numbers and dates into speech is the assistant's job. The services return raw values only, no sentences meant to be read to the caller (the `messageText` in errors is for logs, please don't read it out).
487	
488	## 2. Access token
489	
490	The services sit behind our API gateway. You need a bearer token first.
491	
492	```
493	POST https://api.freyabank.example/oauth2/token
494	Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded
495	
496	grant_type=client_credentials&client_id=<client id>&client_secret=<client secret>&scope=voice.statement
497	```
498	
499	Answer:
500	
501	```json
502	{
503	  "access_token": "<token>",
504	  "token_type": "Bearer",
505	  "expires_in": 1800
506	}
507	```
508	
509	Then on every service call:
510	
511	| Header | Value |
512	|---|---|
513	| `Authorization` | `Bearer <token>` |
514	| `Content-Type` | `application/json` |
515	| `Accept` | `application/json` |
516	
517	The token belongs to the integration (service account), not to the caller. Cache it and get a fresh one when it runs out; don't fetch one per call. Client id and secret: I'll send them over the secure channel, not by e-mail.
518	
519	(Test environment: the token and headers are not checked there. Send them anyway so nothing changes when we switch.)
520	
521	## 3. Envelope
522	
523	### Request
524	
525	```json
526	{
527	  "data": { "...service fields..." },
528	  "call": { "ani": "<caller's number>", "lang": "tr" }
529	}
530	```
531	
532	`data` carries the fields of each service (section 5). `call` is call metadata we log on our side; nothing in this contract depends on it and the test environment ignores it.
533	
534	### Response
535	
536	Every answer has a `result` object. Successful answers also have `data`.
537	
538	```json
539	{
540	  "data": { "...service fields..." },
541	  "result": {
542	    "guid": "f0e1d2c3b4a5968778695a4b3c2d0002",
543	    "returnCode": "1",
544	    "messageText": "Success",
545	    "code": "1",
546	    "message": "Success",
547	    "type": null,
548	    "details": {
549	      "guid": "f0e1d2c3b4a5968778695a4b3c2d0002",
550	      "rootCause": null,
551	      "errorOrigin": null
552	    }
553	  }
554	}
555	```
556	
557	Success = HTTP 200 and `result.returnCode` is `"1"`. Anything else is an error, see section 4. `guid` is our trace id; if you open a ticket with us, give us the `guid`.
558	
559	## 4. Errors
560	
561	Error answers have **no `data` object**, only `result`:
562	
563	```json
564	{
565	  "result": {
566	    "guid": "f0e1d2c3b4a5968778695a4b3c2d0086",
567	    "returnCode": "FBE00099",
568	    "messageText": "Teknik hata: ABORTED: ",
569	    "code": "FBE00099",
570	    "message": "Teknik hata: ABORTED: ",
571	    "type": "ERROR",
572	    "details": {
573	      "guid": "f0e1d2c3b4a5968778695a4b3c2d0086",
574	      "rootCause": "TechnicalError",
575	      "errorOrigin": "ivr-gateway-test:ivr-channel-v0"
576	    }
577	  }
578	}
579	```
580	
581	`returnCode` and `code` always carry the same value, and so do `messageText` and `message`. `type` is `"ERROR"` or `"WARNING"`. `rootCause` and `errorOrigin` are diagnostic strings; log them, don't branch on them.
582	
583	Codes you can get:
584	
585	| HTTP | `code` | `type` | When | Services |
586	|---|---|---|---|---|
587	| 400 | `INVALID_ARGUMENTS_ERROR` | `ERROR` | A required field is missing or empty (message names the field, e.g. `"card number cannot be empty"`) | all |
588	| 401 | (gateway) | | Token missing or expired. Get a new token and retry once | all |
589	| 404 | `FB_IVR_CHANNEL_102` | `WARNING` | Customer has no valid card (message: `"Müşteriye ait geçerli kart bilgisi bulunamadı."`) | `cards.list` |
590	| 404 | `FB_IVR_CHANNEL_120` | `WARNING` | Card not found | `cards.balance` |
591	| 404 | `FB_IVR_CHANNEL_121` | `WARNING` | Card not found | `statement.week.get` |
592	| 404 | `FB_IVR_CHANNEL_107` | `WARNING` | No statement document to send (message: `"Pdf dokümanı bulunamadı"`) | `statement.pdf.send` |
593	| 500 | `FBE00099` | `ERROR` | Technical error on our side (message: `"Teknik hata: ABORTED: "`) | all |
594	
595	Note on the `cards.list` 404: it's a WARNING, it means "this customer has no card the assistant can work with", not that the service is broken. How the assistant reacts to that vs. a 500 is for Selin's analysis, I'm only flagging that they are different things.
596	
597	Timeouts: we haven't agreed a client timeout yet. Most answers are well under a second, but under load (and once in the test data) an answer can take longer than ten seconds and still succeed. Open point, see section 7.
598	
599	## 5. Services

# The final case: Freya Bank, credit card statement debt

Freya Bank is fictional. Every customer, card, amount and address in this pack is synthetic.

## When

The case opens Sunday 11 October, 17:00 UTC (20:00 Istanbul). Submissions close Sunday 11 October, 20:00 UTC (23:00 Istanbul).

## The scenario

Freya Bank wants its phone line to answer one of its most common calls with a voice assistant: "how much is my credit card statement debt?". The caller has already passed the bank's phone menu (IVR). The menu has checked who they are and hands the call to the assistant with the customer number. The assistant finds the right card, reads the statement debt in Turkish lira, US dollars, euros and pounds sterling, and says when it is due.

In the same call the customer may want two more things: move their statement date to another week, or get the statement sent to the e-mail address the bank has on file. A customer who wants to pay or who asks for a person is handed to a human agent. The calls are in Turkish.

The bank did not write a clean specification. It sent what it had: an analysis document, the announcements its phone menu reads today, a flow drawing, service descriptions, an integration document, its mails to our team, a list of abbreviations and an FAQ. They were written months apart and they do not always agree.

## What you build

1. **First, your own mock of the bank's services**, on Cloudflare Workers. Same paths, same field names, same request and response shapes as the bank's integration document (section 6). For the bank's test customers it returns exactly the answers listed in the pack, HTTP status included. Deploy it before you run your builder and keep it running until the results are out: our simulated customers reach your mock through the tools in your workflow, so a Worker that is down fails those conversations.
2. **Then the phone agent, built by your builder.** Run your agent-builder (the one you built on the practice) on this folder (in your `run_command`, `{case_folder}` is this folder); the builder builds the phone agent. No manual edits to what it builds. You may fix bugs in your builder, but do not hard-code this case into it. The phone agent's tools call your mock. It runs on Freya LLM, the only model on staging. Every builder rule on the event page holds here too.

Every call gives the phone agent two variables:

- `customerNumber`: the 8-digit customer number from the phone menu. The agent never asks for it.
- `now`: the date and time of the call, Istanbul time, for example `2026-10-12T10:30:00+03:00`. Every date decision uses `now`, never the system clock.

## Inputs

- `README.md`: the pack overview: what each folder is, the two variables.
- `statement-debt-call-flow.pdf`: a call-flow drawing of the step.
- `sources/emails/`: mail threads between the bank and our team, with the bank's analysis documents in `attachments/`.
- `sources/documents/`: what the bank handed over: the phone-menu prompt sheet, the service contract and a page from the bank's website.
- `sources/meetings/`: transcript excerpts from meetings with the bank.
- `test-environment/`: the bank's test customers (`test-customers.md`, `test-customers.json`) your mock must serve.
- `example-scenarios.md`: six example conversations (two ordinary, two edge, two adversarial) of the kind we score with. The rest stay hidden.
- `cloudflare-mock/`: how to run and deploy a Worker, with a one-endpoint example. The bank's services you write yourself.

## How you are scored

Your phone agent is tested with simulated customers you never see. The workflow your builder made is reviewed too. In the simulations your agent's tools call your mock, so a wrong or unreachable mock fails those conversations. Traces are not scored; we read them to check the agent came out of your builder without hand edits.

## What you submit

One `submission.json`: the workflow your builder made, the trace of that builder run (paths relative to the repo) and the address of your mock.

```json
{
  "team": "Your team name",
  "members": [{ "name": "Ayşe Yılmaz", "email": "ayse@example.com" }],
  "repo": "https://github.com/your-team/your-builder",
  "commit": "the commit you ran",
  "run_command": "the command that runs your builder on this folder",
  "workflow": "submission/final.workflow.json",
  "trace": "traces/final.log",
  "mock_url": "https://your-mock.your-subdomain.workers.dev"
}
```

E-mail `submission.json`, the exported workflow and the trace to yavuz@freyavoice.ai before Sunday 11 October, 20:00 UTC (23:00 Istanbul).

# Mock service with Cloudflare Workers

Your flow's tools call a mock service that you write, instead of the real bank service. You publish this service as a free Cloudflare Worker. The `example/` folder here only shows the pattern: a Worker with a single endpoint (`POST /ping`). You will write the statement-debt services yourself.

## Requirements

- Node.js 18 or later
- A free Cloudflare account (dash.cloudflare.com)
- Wrangler (Cloudflare's command-line tool): runs without installing, via `npx wrangler ...`

## 1. Run the example locally

```bash
cd example
npx wrangler dev
```

The Worker opens at `http://localhost:8787`. Try it from another terminal:

```bash
curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8787/ping \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"kod": "A1"}'
```

The response is the same as `example/example-response.json`. For a code that does not exist it returns `404` and `{"hata": "kayıt bulunamadı"}`.

## 2. Publish it

```bash
npx wrangler login      # grant access to your Cloudflare account in the browser
npx wrangler deploy
```

The output shows the Worker address: `https://example-mock.<your-subdomain>.workers.dev`. To change the name, change the `name` field in `wrangler.toml`. Run `npx wrangler deploy` again whenever the code changes; the address stays the same.

Check after publishing:

```bash
curl -s https://example-mock.<your-subdomain>.workers.dev/health
```

## 3. Connect the tool in the Freya flow to the Worker

1. Add an API tool to the flow.
2. Enter the method and address: `POST https://<your-worker-name>.<your-subdomain>.workers.dev/<path>`. For the statement services, use the same path as under the bank's base address in `../sources/documents/2026-10-01-service-contract.md` (for example `/voice/v1/cards.list`).
3. In the request body, write variables in the form `{{variable_name}}`. Example: `{"data": {"customerNo": "{{customerNumber}}", "aiFlow": "..."}, "call": {...}}`. During the call, the variable's value is substituted in.
4. Take the fields you will use in the flow from the response into variables.

The "Test API Request" button in the panel may send the text `{{customerNumber}}` as is, without filling in the variables. In this case the example Worker returns a valid record instead of an error (`isTemplateVariable`). Doing the same in your own services makes testing easier.

## When writing your own services

- Endpoints, request and response fields must match `../sources/documents/2026-10-01-service-contract.md` exactly: the same path, the same field names (`data`/`call` request body, `data`/`result` response), the same date and amount format. The test customers' responses are in `../test-environment/test-customers.json`, explained in `../test-environment/test-customers.md`.
- Keep customer and card data in a table inside the Worker file (like `RECORDS` in the example). No database is needed.
- For a customer or card that is not found, return the error response from the contract; do not return made-up data.
- Responses should return data only (amount, date, status). The flow builds the sentence to be said to the customer.
- Do not put secret keys or real personal data in it; the Worker address is public.

// Example Cloudflare Worker: a standalone mock service with a single endpoint.
// POST /ping  body: { "kod": "A1" }  ->  returns a record from the table in this file.
// This file only shows the pattern; you will write the statement-debt services yourself.

const RECORDS = {
  A1: { kod: "A1", ad: "Örnek kayıt", tutar: 1250.5, tarih: "15.11.2026" },
  B2: { kod: "B2", ad: "İkinci kayıt", tutar: 0, tarih: "01.12.2026" },
};

const CORS = { "Access-Control-Allow-Origin": "*" };

function json(body, status = 200) {
  return Response.json(body, { status: status, headers: CORS });
}

async function readBody(request) {
  try { return await request.json(); } catch { return null; }
}

// The panel's "Test API Request" button sends variables without filling them in, e.g. "{{kod}}".
function isTemplateVariable(value) {
  return typeof value === "string" && (value.startsWith("{{") || value.startsWith("%7B%7B"));
}

async function ping(request) {
  const body = (await readBody(request)) || {};
  if (isTemplateVariable(body.kod)) return json(RECORDS.A1);
  const record = RECORDS[String(body.kod || "").trim()];
  if (!record) return json({ hata: "kayıt bulunamadı" }, 404);
  return json(record);
}

export default {
  async fetch(request) {
    const url = new URL(request.url);
    if (request.method === "OPTIONS") {
      return new Response(null, { headers: {
        ...CORS,
        "Access-Control-Allow-Methods": "GET, POST, OPTIONS",
        "Access-Control-Allow-Headers": "*",
      } });
    }
    if (request.method === "GET" && url.pathname === "/health") return json({ durum: "ok" });
    if (request.method === "POST" && url.pathname === "/ping") return ping(request);
    return json({ hata: "bulunamadı", yollar: ["GET /health", "POST /ping"] }, 404);
  },
};
